examples.en: There is a storytelling hour at the library.

examples.ko: 선생님이 목소리를 바꿔 가며 구연동화를 해 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher told us a story, changing her voice as she went.

examples.ko: 아이들이 구연동화에 푹 빠져서 조용히 앉아 있어요.
examples.en: The children are so absorbed in the storytelling that they sit quietly.

examples.ko: 저는 주말마다 유치원에서 구연동화 봉사를 해요.
examples.en: Every weekend I volunteer doing storytelling at a kindergarten.
When the storytelling ended, the children clapped.
There are also classes that teach English through storytelling.

explain: 책을 그대로 읽어 주는 것과 달리, 목소리와 표정, 몸짓으로 이야기를 생생하게 들려주는 것을 말해요. 도서관, 유치원, 어린이 행사에서 많이 접해요. '구연동화를 하다', '구연동화 시간'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: A volunteer tells fairy tales to the children.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이야기를 들려주는 사람이 주어일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the storyteller is the subject.

phrases.en: The children laughed after listening to the storytelling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 듣는 사람 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the listener's side.
phrases.en_equiv: to listen to a told story

phrases.en: A storytelling contest is being held this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실력을 겨루는 행사 이름에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attached to the names of events where people compete.

explain_en: Unlike simply reading a book aloud, it means telling a story vividly using voice, facial expressions, and gestures. You meet it at libraries, kindergartens, and children's events. People say '구연동화를 하다' or '구연동화 시간'.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 팀에서 가장 수비가 좋은 내야수예요.
examples.en: That player is the infielder with the best defense on the team.
The infielder caught the ball and threw it to first base.
My son plays infielder in baseball.
Infielders and outfielders do different jobs.

examples.ko: 새로 온 내야수는 첫 경기에서 안타를 쳤어요.
examples.en: The new infielder got a hit in his first game.
The infielders have gathered at the mound and are talking.

explain: 반대말은 '외야수'예요. 1루수, 2루수, 3루수, 유격수를 합쳐서 부르는 말이고, 야구 중계나 뉴스에서 자주 들려요. 한 명이든 여러 명이든 쓰고, 여러 명일 때는 '내야수들'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The infielders pass the ball quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 명일 때 '들'을 붙여요. 경기 중계에서 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '들' for more than one person. Often heard in game broadcasts.

phrases.example: 올해 들어온 신인 내야수가 수비를 잘해요.
phrases.en: The rookie infielder who joined this year plays good defense.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선수 소개에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요. 팀에 새로 들어온 선수를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing in player introductions. Used for a newly joined player.

phrases.example: 내야수와 외야수는 서 있는 위치가 달라요.
phrases.en: Infielders and outfielders stand in different positions.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말인 '외야수'와 나란히 쓰면 야구 포지션을 설명하기 쉬워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Using it alongside its opposite '외야수' makes baseball positions easy to explain.

explain_en: The opposite is '외야수' (outfielder). It is the collective term for the first, second and third basemen and the shortstop, and you hear it often in baseball broadcasts and news. It works for one player or several; for several you can say '내야수들'.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 텔레비전에서 단막극을 자주 봤어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I often watched one-act dramas on TV.

examples.ko: 이 단막극은 한 시간 만에 끝나서 보기 편해요.
examples.en: This one-act drama ends in an hour, so it's easy to watch.

examples.ko: 단막극 한 편으로 신인 배우가 유명해졌어요.
examples.en: The newcomer actor became famous through a single one-act drama.

examples.ko: 학교 축제에서 우리 반이 단막극을 올렸어요.
examples.en: At the school festival, our class staged a one-act play.
One-act dramas have become rare these days, which is a pity.

examples.ko: 그 단막극에서 아버지 역을 맡은 배우가 최고였어요.
examples.en: The actor who played the father in that one-act drama was the best.

explain: 한 편으로 끝나는 짧은 극이라서, 여러 회로 이어지는 '연속극'과 자주 비교돼요. 연극 무대보다는 텔레비전 드라마 이야기에서 더 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: I watched a one-act drama on TV on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짧은 드라마를 한 편 볼 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic way to say you watched a short, single-episode drama.

phrases.en: It would be nice to make this story into a one-act play.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이야기를 한 편짜리 극으로 만든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means turning a story into a single-episode play.
phrases.en_equiv: to turn into a one-act play

phrases.en: TV one-act dramas have short, fun stories.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단막극이 주로 텔레비전 드라마에서 쓰인다는 것을 보여 주는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing that shows the word is mostly used for TV dramas.

explain_en: Because it finishes in a single episode, it is often contrasted with '연속극' (a serial drama). You hear it more in talk about TV dramas than about stage plays.

examples.en: I heard Korea has been known since long ago as the land of courtesy in the East.

examples.ko: 어른께 인사도 안 하다니 동방예의지국이 맞나 싶어요.
examples.en: Not even greeting an elder, I wonder if this is really the 'land of courtesy'.
True to the 'land of courtesy', I offered the elder a seat first.
Foreigners find it interesting when they hear the term 'land of courtesy in the East'.

examples.ko: 요즘 동방예의지국의 예절이 많이 달라졌다고 해요.
examples.en: They say the manners of the 'land of courtesy' have changed a lot lately.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 동방예의지국 소리를 들은 게 자랑이라고 하세요.
examples.en: Grandfather says he is proud that Korea was called the 'land of courtesy'.

explain: 우리나라가 예의 바른 나라라고 불렸다는 오래된 자랑스러운 표현이에요. 요즘은 예의 없는 행동을 보고 '동방예의지국 맞아?'처럼 비꼬듯 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: Korea has been called the 'Eastern Land of Courtesy' since long ago.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이 말이 나라의 별명이었다고 설명할 때 이렇게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to say that a country was known by this nickname.
phrases.en_equiv: to be called the land of courtesy

phrases.example: 어른이 서 계신데 자리도 안 비켜 주다니, 동방예의지국 맞아요?
phrases.en: How can they not give up a seat when an elder is standing? Is this really the land of courtesy?
phrases.nuance_ko: 예의 없는 행동을 보고 비꼬듯 물어볼 때 쓰는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A sarcastic question you ask when you see rude behavior.
phrases.en_equiv: Is this really the land of courtesy?

phrases.example: 동방예의지국답게 우리는 어른께 물건을 두 손으로 드려요.
phrases.en: True to the land of courtesy, we hand things to elders with both hands.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예의 바른 행동을 자랑스럽게 말할 때 '-답게'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-답게' to talk proudly about polite behavior.
phrases.en_equiv: true to the land of courtesy

explain_en: It is an old, proud expression saying Korea was known as a courteous country. These days people also use it sarcastically when they see rude behavior, as in '동방예의지국 맞아?'.

examples.en: This song is a classic that has been loved for a long time.
We listened together to the classic songs my father likes.
I bought a collection of that singer's best songs.
Great songs keep being sung even as time passes.
A classic song from the 80s came on the radio.
At karaoke I picked and sang only classics.

explain: 명곡은 오래 사랑받아 온 훌륭한 노래에 써요. 요즘 인기 있는 노래는 '인기곡', 크게 유행한 노래는 '히트곡'이라고 해요. '명작', '명화'처럼 '명-'이 붙으면 훌륭한 작품이라는 느낌이 돼요.

phrases.example: 비 오는 날에는 옛날 명곡을 들어요.
phrases.en: On rainy days I listen to classic songs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래 사랑받은 노래를 찾아 듣는다는 느낌으로 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the feeling of seeking out well-loved songs to listen to.

phrases.example: 이 노래는 제가 생각하는 최고의 명곡이에요.
phrases.en: This is the best classic song in my opinion.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 훌륭하다고 생각하는 노래를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the song you think is the greatest of all.

phrases.en: This movie is a masterpiece that is remembered for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '명-'이 붙은 말이에요. 명곡은 노래에, 명작은 영화·책·그림 같은 작품에 두루 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Another 명- word: 명곡 is for songs, while 명작 is for works like films, books, and art.

explain_en: 명곡 is for a great song that has been loved for years. A currently popular song is '인기곡', and a big hit is '히트곡'. The prefix '명-' as in '명작' and '명화' adds the sense of an excellent work.

examples.ko: 아버지는 대학 시절 민중가요를 자주 부르셨대요.
examples.en: I heard my father often sang people's songs in his college days.

examples.ko: 이 민중가요는 시위 현장에서 많이 불렸어요.
examples.en: This protest song was sung a lot at demonstrations.

examples.ko: 이번 주말에 민중가요 콘서트에 같이 갈래요?
examples.en: Do you want to go to a minjung song concert this weekend?

examples.ko: 민중가요의 가사에는 사회에 대한 메시지가 담겨 있어요.
examples.en: The lyrics of minjung songs carry messages about society.
The teacher played a minjung song during class.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 민중가요를 현대적으로 다시 불렀어요.
examples.en: That singer sang a minjung song again in a modern style.

explain: 일반 유행가와 달리 사회와 시대 이야기를 담은 노래라는 느낌이 강해요. 한국의 민주화 운동 시기와 함께 자주 언급돼요. '민중가요를 부르다', '민중가요를 듣다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: I sometimes listen to old minjung songs.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부르다'가 직접 노래하는 것이라면 '듣다'는 감상하는 쪽이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: While 부르다 is singing it yourself, 듣다 is listening to it.

phrases.en: He was a famous minjung song singer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 민중가요를 주로 부르는 가수를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This refers to a singer who mainly sings minjung songs.

phrases.example: 민중가요 가사에는 시대의 아픔이 담겨 있어요.
phrases.en: The lyrics of minjung songs carry the pain of their era.
phrases.nuance_ko: 노래의 내용과 메시지를 이야기할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when talking about the content and message of the songs.

explain_en: Unlike ordinary pop songs, it feels like a song carrying society and the times. It is often mentioned together with Korea's democratization movement. It goes with '민중가요를 부르다' (sing) and '민중가요를 듣다' (listen).

examples.en: I hit the drum hard with the drumstick.
I lost my drumstick, so I couldn't practice.

examples.ko: 공연 전에 북채를 두 개 준비했어요.
examples.en: I prepared two drumsticks before the performance.

examples.ko: 아이에게 북채를 쥐는 법을 가르쳐 줬어요.
examples.en: I taught the child how to hold a drumstick.
The drumstick broke, so I bought a new one.

examples.ko: 선생님이 북채를 높이 들고 박자를 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: The teacher raised the drumstick high and showed us the beat.

explain: 풍물놀이나 판소리의 북처럼 한국 전통 북을 치는 막대를 말할 때 자연스러워요. 서양 드럼에는 보통 '드럼 스틱'이라고 해요. '북을 치다'와 함께 '북채를 잡다'라고 자주 말해요.

phrases.example: 그는 북채를 잡고 크게 숨을 쉬었어요.
phrases.en: He took the drumstick and breathed deeply.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연주를 시작하기 전 모습을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for the moment before starting to play.

phrases.en: The child beats the drum energetically with the drumstick.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도구와 행동을 함께 말하는 기본 문장이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A basic phrase that names both the tool and the action.
phrases.en_equiv: to beat a drum with a drumstick

phrases.en: When the performance ended, he put down the drumsticks and bowed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연주를 마치고 북채를 내려놓을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when putting the drumsticks down after playing.

explain_en: It sounds natural for the stick used on traditional Korean drums, such as in pungmul or pansori. For a Western drum set, people usually say '드럼 스틱'. Along with '북을 치다' (to beat a drum), you often hear '북채를 잡다' (to pick up the sticks).

examples.ko: 어릴 때 골목에서 친구들과 사방치기를 했어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I played hopscotch with my friends in the alley.
I drew the hopscotch squares on the ground with chalk.

examples.ko: 사방치기는 한 발로 뛰면서 하는 놀이예요.
examples.en: Hopscotch is a game where you hop on one foot.
I stepped on a line while playing hopscotch, so I lost.
Do kids these days know hopscotch too?

examples.ko: 사방치기 돌을 던져 칸 안에 정확히 넣었어요.
examples.en: I threw the hopscotch stone and landed it exactly inside the square.

explain: 땅에 칸을 그리고 한 발로 뛰며 노는 놀이로, 영어의 hopscotch와 거의 같아요. 어릴 때 놀던 추억을 이야기할 때 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The children play hopscotch at lunchtime.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀이를 한다는 가장 기본적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic way to say someone plays the game.

phrases.example: 사방치기 놀이는 한 발로 뛰어서 해요.
phrases.en: Hopscotch is played by hopping on one foot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀이 이름으로 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain the game by name.

phrases.en: I drew big hopscotch squares with chalk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀이를 하려고 바닥에 그리는 칸을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the squares drawn on the ground for the game.

explain_en: It is a game where you draw squares on the ground and hop through them on one foot, almost the same as English hopscotch. It often comes up when people talk about childhood memories.

en: being lost; being absorbed; being immersed

examples.ko: 동생은 게임 삼매경에 빠져서 불러도 몰라요.
examples.en: My brother is so absorbed in his game that he doesn't notice when I call.

examples.ko: 공부 삼매경인 학생들 때문에 도서관이 조용했어요.
examples.en: The library was quiet because the students were deeply absorbed in studying.

examples.ko: 삼매경에 빠진 아이 옆에서 조용히 간식을 놓았어요.
examples.en: I quietly put a snack next to the child, who was lost in what he was doing.

examples.ko: 그는 요리 삼매경이라서 전화도 안 받아요.
examples.en: He is so lost in cooking that he doesn't even answer the phone.
Everyone on the subway is absorbed in their phones.

examples.ko: 한참 낚시 삼매경에 빠져 있다가 해가 진 걸 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I was so absorbed in fishing that I didn't notice the sun had set.

explain: 앞에 게임, 독서, 낚시처럼 하는 일을 붙여서 '~삼매경'이라고 말해요. '삼매경에 빠지다'가 가장 자연스러운 짝이에요. '몰두하다'보다 말하듯 편하게 쓰는 표현이에요.

phrases.en: My older brother gets lost in reading every weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '삼매경' 앞에 하는 일을 붙여서 그 일에 푹 빠진 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the activity before 삼매경 to describe being completely absorbed in it.

phrases.en: The kids got totally absorbed in playing with blocks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 자연스러운 짝말이에요. 무엇에 푹 빠져서 다른 것이 안 보일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural collocation; use it when someone is so absorbed that they notice nothing else.

phrases.example: 아버지는 낚시 삼매경이라서 전화도 안 받으세요.
phrases.en: My father is so absorbed in fishing that he doesn't even answer the phone.
phrases.nuance_ko: '빠지다' 없이 '~삼매경이다'로도 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: You can also say '~삼매경이다' without '빠지다'.

explain_en: You put the activity before it, as in 게임, 독서 or 낚시 plus 삼매경. '삼매경에 빠지다' is its most natural pairing. It sounds more casual and conversational than '몰두하다'.

examples.ko: 친구가 선생님 성대모사를 해서 다 웃었어요.
examples.en: My friend did an impression of the teacher and everyone laughed.
I envy people who are good at impersonating voices.

examples.ko: 그 가수 성대모사 좀 해 보세요.
examples.en: Do an impression of that singer for us.
My child keeps imitating the cartoon character's voice.
I laughed for a long time watching a voice impression video.
The voice is so similar that the impression sounds real.

explain: 다른 사람이나 동물의 목소리를 똑같이 흉내 내는 것에 써요. '성대모사(를) 하다'라고 하고, '흉내 내다'는 목소리뿐 아니라 동작까지 포함할 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 그 개그맨은 유명한 가수의 성대모사를 해요.
phrases.en: That comedian imitates a famous singer's voice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표제어와 함께 가장 많이 쓰는 기본 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic collocation with the headword.

phrases.en: My older brother is good at doing impressions.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실력을 칭찬하거나 소개할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise or introduce someone's skill.

phrases.example: 아이가 만화 주인공의 목소리를 흉내 내요.
phrases.en: The child imitates the voice of the cartoon character.
phrases.nuance_ko: '성대모사'를 풀어서 쉽게 말한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler way of saying 성대모사.

explain_en: It is for copying another person's or animal's voice closely, used as '성대모사(를) 하다'. '흉내 내다' can cover not just voice but also actions.

examples.en: This band became famous by performing on the street.
A band played live at the wedding.
I went to see a performance by an old orchestra.
My uncle plays the trumpet in a small band.
I heard a new conductor joined that orchestra.
The band and the singer went on stage together.

explain: 음악을 연주하는 사람들의 단체를 두루 부르는 말이라 오케스트라와 밴드에 모두 쓸 수 있어요. 일상 대화에서는 '밴드'나 '오케스트라'라고 더 많이 말하고, '악단'은 뉴스나 글에서 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: Our school band performed at the festival.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '악단'보다 '밴드'를 더 많이 써요. 기타나 드럼이 있는 팀에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: In everyday talk 밴드 is more common than 악단, especially for groups with guitars and drums.

phrases.example: 악단 단원들이 무대에 올라 악기를 조율했어요.
phrases.en: The orchestra members went on stage and tuned their instruments.
phrases.nuance_ko: 악단에 속한 사람들을 말할 때 '단원'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 단원 to refer to the people who belong to the group.

phrases.en: He has led the orchestra for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지휘자나 대표가 악단을 맡아 운영한다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a conductor or leader runs and guides the group.

explain_en: It broadly names a group of people who play music, so it can fit both an orchestra and a band. In daily talk people more often say '밴드' or '오케스트라', and '악단' shows up more in news and writing.

examples.en: I danced with my shoulders while listening to the song.
When Dad is in a good mood, he starts moving his shoulders to a beat.
My shoulders start dancing on their own to the market music.
Grandfather sang while swaying his shoulders.
Even just moving your shoulders makes it feel lively.

examples.ko: 합격 소식에 동생이 어깨춤을 추면서 방을 돌았어요.
examples.en: At the news of passing, my younger sibling went around the room dancing with shoulders swaying.

explain: 신이 나서 어깨를 들썩이며 추는 춤이에요. '어깨춤을 추다' 또는 '어깨춤이 나다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I felt like dancing when I heard about my promotion.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기쁜 일이 있어서 몸이 저절로 들썩일 만큼 신이 날 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively when something makes you so happy that you feel like dancing.
phrases.en_equiv: to feel like dancing for joy

explain_en: It is a dance where you bounce your shoulders in excitement. It is used as '어깨춤을 추다' or '어깨춤이 나다'.

en: to be published serially; to be serialized

examples.en: This comic is serialized on the website every week.

examples.ko: 그 소설은 신문에 일 년 동안 연재됐어요.
examples.en: That novel ran serially in the newspaper for a year.

examples.ko: 새 웹툰이 다음 주부터 연재될 거예요.
examples.en: The new webtoon will start serializing next week.
Waiting for the serialized story is fun.
They collected the serialized pieces and published a book.
A cooking column is being serialized in a magazine.

explain: 만화, 소설, 글을 한 번에 다 내지 않고 정해진 날마다 조금씩 싣는 것을 말해요. '웹툰이 연재되다'처럼 작품이 주어예요. 쓰는 사람은 '연재하다'를 써요. 끝나면 '완결되다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: This webtoon is still being serialized.
phrases.nuance_ko: '중'은 지금 계속되고 있다는 뜻이라서 끝나지 않은 작품에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '중' means it's ongoing, used for works that haven't ended.

phrases.en: That novel is serialized in the newspaper every week.
phrases.nuance_ko: '매주', '매일'처럼 정해진 때와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used together with set times like 'every week' or 'every day'.

phrases.en: That comic's serialization ended last month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '연재'를 써서 작품이 끝났다는 걸 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun '연재' to say the series has ended.

explain_en: It describes comics, novels, or writing being released bit by bit on set days instead of all at once. The work is the subject, as in '웹툰이 연재되다'. The creator uses 연재하다, and when it ends it is 완결되다.

examples.en: The crowd chants the player's name.
The fans waited, chanting the singer's name.
The protesters are chanting slogans.
Everyone stood up and chanted 'Hooray'.

examples.ko: 사람들이 그의 이름을 연호하자 그는 손을 흔들었어요.
examples.en: When people chanted his name, he waved his hand.

examples.ko: 경기장 전체가 응원 구호를 연호하니까 소름이 돋았어요.
examples.en: The whole stadium chanted the cheer, and I got goosebumps.

explain: 같은 말이나 이름을 여러 사람이 계속 소리쳐 부를 때 써요. 일상에서는 '외치다', '이름을 부르다'가 더 자연스럽고, '연호하다'는 뉴스나 글에서 많이 나와요. 보통 '이름을 연호하다', '구호를 연호하다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: The citizens chanted the slogan in one voice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집회나 응원에서 같은 말을 반복해 외칠 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when repeatedly shouting the same words at rallies or cheering.

phrases.en: The sound of chanting was loud in the stadium.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 명사 '소리'를 꾸미는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-는' form modifying the noun '소리'.

phrases.en: The crowd shouted the player's name loudly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '연호하다'와 비슷하지만 일상에서 더 자연스럽게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 연호하다 but sounds more natural in daily conversation.

explain_en: It is used when many people keep shouting the same word or name. In daily speech, '외치다' or '이름을 부르다' sounds more natural, while '연호하다' appears more in news and writing. It is usually used as '이름을 연호하다' or '구호를 연호하다'.

en: catching a big fish; big fish

examples.ko: 월척 한 마리 잡는 게 이번 낚시의 목표예요.
examples.en: My goal for this fishing trip is to catch one really big fish.
My father sent a photo saying he caught a big fish.

examples.ko: 오늘은 월척은커녕 한 마리도 못 잡았어요.
examples.en: Today I didn't even catch one fish, let alone a big one.

examples.ko: 월척이다! 이렇게 큰 물고기는 처음 봐요.
examples.en: What a catch! I've never seen such a big fish.
The fishing spot buzzed at the news of a big catch.

examples.ko: 이번 낚시 대회에서는 월척이 여러 마리 나왔어요.
examples.en: Several big fish were caught at this fishing contest.

explain: 낚시에서 크게 자란 물고기를 잡았을 때 쓰는 말이에요. 비유로 좋은 사람이나 큰 성과를 얻었을 때 '월척을 낚았다'고 농담처럼 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: I finally caught a big fish today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 낚시뿐 아니라 좋은 사람이나 성과를 얻었을 때 비유로도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for fishing and also figuratively for a great catch or result.

phrases.en: Wow, this is a big one!
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 물고기를 보고 놀라며 칭찬할 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said in admiration when you see a big fish.

phrases.en: I lost the big fish that was on my line.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 기회를 아깝게 놓쳤다는 비유로도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can also mean narrowly missing a big opportunity.

explain_en: It is a fishing word for catching a big fish. Jokingly, people also say '월척을 낚았다' for landing a great person or a big achievement.

examples.en: We sang the cheering songs loudly at the baseball stadium.
This cheering song gives me energy when I hear it.
A new cheering song became popular during the World Cup.

examples.ko: 우리 반은 체육 대회를 위해 응원가를 만들었어요.
examples.en: Our class made a cheering song for the sports day.
I went after memorizing all the cheering song lyrics.
Each player has their own cheering song.

explain: '응원가'는 한국 야구장이나 축구장에서 관중이 같이 부르는 노래를 말해요. 선수 한 명마다 따로 있는 응원가도 있어서 팬들이 외워서 불러요. 시험 보는 친구를 응원하는 노래는 보통 '응원 노래'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: I made a cheering song for my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '응원가'와 뜻은 비슷하지만 야구장 노래뿐 아니라 개인을 응원할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 응원가, but also used when cheering for a person.

phrases.en: The fans all sing the cheering song together.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부르다'와 함께 쓰는 가장 기본적인 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic usage, with 부르다.

phrases.en: I memorized the lyrics of the cheering song.
phrases.nuance_ko: 노래의 말 부분을 이야기할 때 '가사'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 가사 to talk about the words of the song.

explain_en: 응원가 is a song the crowd sings together at Korean baseball or soccer stadiums. Some players even have their own, and fans memorize them. A song to cheer on a friend taking an exam would usually be called 응원 노래.

en: writing (of a book); authorship; a written work

examples.en: The professor devoted a whole life to writing books.

examples.ko: 그의 저술은 지금도 많은 사람이 읽어요.
examples.en: His writings are still read by many people today.

examples.ko: 오랜 저술 끝에 책이 드디어 나왔어요.
examples.en: After a long period of writing, the book finally came out.

examples.ko: 저술 활동을 하면서 강의도 계속하고 있어요.
examples.en: I keep lecturing while doing my writing work.

examples.ko: 이 저술에는 십 년 동안의 연구가 담겨 있어요.
examples.en: This work contains ten years of research.

examples.ko: 저술을 도와줄 조교를 한 명 구하고 있어요.
examples.en: I am looking for an assistant who can help with my writing.

explain: 책이나 논문처럼 꽤 긴 글을 쓰는 일, 또는 그렇게 쓴 책을 가리켜요. 편하게 쓰는 '글쓰기'에 비해 학자나 작가의 공식적인 작업에 쓰는 딱딱한 말이에요. '저술 활동', '저술에 힘쓰다'처럼 말해요. 일기나 메시지에는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.example: 교수님은 은퇴 후에도 저술 활동을 계속하세요.
phrases.en: The professor continues writing activities even after retiring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학자나 작가가 책을 쓰는 일을 말할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing often used for scholars or authors writing books.

phrases.en: He left behind many written works.
phrases.nuance_ko: 저술이 책 자체를 뜻할 때의 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A use where 저술 means the written works themselves.

phrases.en: He is famous as an author.
phrases.nuance_ko: 책을 쓰는 일이 직업인 사람을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a person whose work is writing books.

explain_en: It refers to writing something long like a book or paper, or to the book itself. Compared with the casual '글쓰기', it is a stiff word for the formal work of scholars and authors. Typical uses are '저술 활동' and '저술에 힘쓰다'. You would not use it for a diary or a message.

dis.h: authoring serious books; also the work itself

p.n: The swap stresses the act of writing; the original stresses authoring scholarly works.

examples.ko: 이 작가의 새 소설이 다음 주에 출간돼요.
examples.en: This author's new novel is being published next week.

examples.ko: 그 책은 십 년 전에 출간됐어요.
examples.en: That book was published ten years ago.

examples.ko: 번역본이 출간되면 꼭 사서 읽을 거예요.
examples.en: When the translation is published, I'll definitely buy and read it.
The poetry collection published this time is popular in bookstores.
A signing event is held on the day the book is published.

examples.ko: 외국에서 먼저 출간된 뒤에 한국에도 들어왔어요.
examples.en: It was first published abroad and then came to Korea.

explain: 책이 세상에 나올 때 써요. 신문이나 잡지 같은 정기 간행물은 '발행되다', 책은 '출간되다', '출판되다'를 써요. '출간되다'는 막 나온 새 책 소식에 특히 자주 써요.

phrases.en: That novel was published this spring.
phrases.nuance_ko: '출간되다'와 거의 같은 뜻이지만 책을 만들어 내는 일 전체를 가리키는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same as 출간되다, but it feels like the whole process of producing a book.

phrases.en: I want to buy the book that came out yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갓 나온 책을 꾸미는 모양으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used as a modifier for a newly released book.

phrases.example: 그 작가의 새 책이 다음 달에 나와요.
phrases.en: The author's new book comes out next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '출간되다' 대신 쉽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday way to say 출간되다.

explain_en: Used when a book comes out into the world. Periodicals like newspapers and magazines are 발행되다, while books are 출간되다 or 출판되다. 출간되다 is especially common for news of a newly released book.

dis.h: a book comes out; common in publisher news

p.n: Almost the same; 출판 is the more general word.

examples.en: The sound of the harp is really clear and soft.
I want to learn the harp someday.

examples.ko: 무대 가운데에 큰 하프가 놓여 있었어요.
examples.en: A big harp was placed in the middle of the stage.
The harpist slowly plucked the strings.
This piece is played on the harp and the piano.
A harp is large, so it's hard to move.

explain: 발음이 같은 '하프(half)'는 '하프타임'처럼 절반을 뜻하는 다른 말이라서 문맥으로 구분해요. 악기 하프는 손가락으로 줄을 튕겨 소리를 내며 '하프를 연주하다'라고 말해요. 활로 줄을 켜는 바이올린과는 소리를 내는 방법이 달라요.

phrases.en: She plays the harp on stage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 악기 하프와 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing with the instrument.

phrases.en: Hearing the harp makes me feel calm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 악기의 소리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the sound of the instrument.

phrases.en: I learn the harp every weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 악기를 공부한다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you are studying the instrument.

explain_en: The identically pronounced 하프 (half) is a different word meaning 'half', as in 하프타임, so context tells them apart. The harp is played by plucking the strings with the fingers, and you say 하프를 연주하다. This differs from the violin, whose strings are played with a bow.

examples.en: At today's concert they'll play a piano concerto.
That violinist played a Beethoven concerto.
A concerto is played by a soloist and an orchestra together.
I study while listening to a Mozart concerto.

examples.ko: 이 협주곡의 마지막 악장이 제일 빨라요.
examples.en: The last movement of this concerto is the fastest.
I like symphonies more than concertos.

explain: '피아노 협주곡', '바이올린 협주곡'처럼 악기 이름이 앞에 와요. 혼자 연주하는 '독주곡'이나 여러 악기가 함께하는 '교향곡'과 달라요. 한국어로는 '콘체르토'보다 '협주곡'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I like piano concertos.
phrases.nuance_ko: 악기 이름이 앞에 오는 가장 흔한 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common use, with the instrument name first.

phrases.en: I listened to a violin concerto today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 악기 이름으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: You can swap in other instrument names.

phrases.en: The orchestra plays a concerto.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공연 장면에서 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used in concert settings.

explain_en: The instrument name comes first, as in '피아노 협주곡' and '바이올린 협주곡'. It differs from a solo piece, '독주곡', and from a symphony, '교향곡'. In Korean people say '협주곡' rather than '콘체르토'.
